Subject: Audit & access logs — export windows and retention?

Hi Ben,

We're evaluating Redwood for a production deployment and have a few detailed questions about audit and access logs before we move forward:

- What are the default retention windows for audit (admin/config) logs vs API access logs in the hosted product? Are these configurable for Dedicated/Private customers?
- Can we continuously export logs to our S3 bucket (or GCS)? If so, what formats do you support (NDJSON, CSV)? Is export delivery guaranteed or best-effort?
- Is there a way to avoid exporting request/response bodies (we only need metadata / headers)? Any automatic PII redaction options?
- For data subject deletion requests, how do you handle audit/access log entries that contain identifiers? Is there a documented process?
- Residency: are logs stored in the tenant region, and can exports be pinned to a region-specific bucket?

Could you point me to a sample export file as well? Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Jamie Ortiz

Subject: Re: Audit & access logs — export windows and retention?

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I'll loop in security/product for specifics and examples:

- Defaults: hosted audit logs ~12 months; hosted access logs ~90 days. Yes — Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer retention.
- Export: continuous export to customer buckets (S3/GCS/Azure) is supported; formats: NDJSON (preferred) and compressed CSV. Delivery is streaming to your bucket; SLA varies by deployment tier.
- Bodies: the default export is metadata-only (timestamp, request path, status, caller ID, IP, user agent). Request/response bodies are not exported by default unless you enable them.
- Deletion: we support purging stored logs per retention TTL and assist with deletion requests; exported objects in your bucket are your responsibility, but we can coordinate.
- Residency: logs are stored in the tenant region and exports can be configured to target a same-region bucket.

I'm attaching a quickstart for S3 export and will pass this to Maya for the detailed export schema and Steph for legal/BAA-related details. Would a 30-min sync tomorrow (Aug 18) at 10am PT work?

Attachments: s3-export-quickstart.pdf

Hi Jamie — following up with the granular details you asked for. I've summarized per log class and included export behavior below.

Audit logs (admin/config changes / RBAC events):
- Hosted default retention: 12 months.
- Dedicated/Private: configurable retention up to 36 months (contract-dependent).
- Schema: structured NDJSON with actor, action, resource, before/after (redacted), and trace_id. Sample schema attached.

Access logs (API calls / inference requests metadata):
- Hosted default retention: 90 days.
- Dedicated/Private: up to 24 months configurable.
- Export contents by default: timestamp, route, model_id, token_count, latency_ms, response_status, caller_id (customer-provided), client_ip (anonymizable), user_agent.

Export and delivery notes:
- Continuous export: yes — streaming to your cloud storage (S3/GCS/Azure) in your account. Supported formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) or compressed CSV (gzip).
- Delivery model: we write objects to your bucket with a time-partitioned prefix (YYYY/MM/DD/HH). For Hosted customers, delivery is best-effort with retries; for Dedicated we offer a contractual delivery SLA (can be included in a Dedicated SOW).
- Exported response bodies: NOT included by default. If a customer opts in to include full request/response payloads (rare), this is controlled by a per-route setting and requires an explicit security review.

Residency and encryption:
- Logs are stored in the tenant's configured region (we do not replicate hosted log data cross-region unless requested). Export targets should be region-aligned to avoid egress.
- All exported objects are server-side encrypted (SSE) and can be delivered encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Deletion and DSARs (Data Subject Access/Deletion Requests):
- For logs stored in Redwood: we honor retention TTLs and can run targeted purges for identifiers where feasible. We maintain an internal audit trail of deletion actions.
- For logs already exported to customer buckets: Redwood cannot delete objects in your bucket. We can provide a manifest (object keys + timestamps) to assist with deletion, or, with explicit permission and an approved process, coordinate deletion on your behalf.
- PII redaction: we provide a redaction pipeline for common fields (email, SSN-like patterns, IP anonymization) that can be applied at export-time for Dedicated/Private customers.

Attached: redwood-log-export-schema.json (sample schema / field descriptions).

If you want, we can prepare a short sample NDJSON file showing a day's worth of partitioned exports.

Subject: Re: Audit & access logs — export windows and retention? (legal)

Hi Jamie — looping in legal perspective on two points you raised. Short answers:

- SLA and retries: for Hosted we operate on a best-effort delivery with exponential backoff and 5 retry windows over ~24 hours before emitting an export failure event to the tenant and support. Typical latency is a few minutes to a couple hours depending on routing and batching. For Dedicated we can contract a delivery SLA and define retry/alerting windows.
- Identifiers & pseudonymization: by default exported caller_id is the customer-provided identifier (not Redwood global identifiers). If you want pseudonymization we can implement a deterministic hash transformation at export time (salted, reversible only with a customer-managed mapping if requested). This is an engineering change that we can scope for Dedicated customers.
- Coordinated deletion from customer buckets: Redwood does not automatically delete customer-owned objects. If you grant a limited-role service account and follow our documented change control + joint runbook, we can perform coordinated deletions and produce an auditable manifest showing object keys deleted, who authorized the deletion, and a timestamp. This would be accompanied by our change control ticket and a signed statement of actions.

HIPAA and BAA: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered workflows through Private deployment or a Dedicated arrangement with a BAA/controls in place. We do not recommend exporting full PHI into hosted buckets without a BAA and explicit controls. Our standard BAA template is attached for review.

Happy to walk through these items on a call.

Best regards,
